Job 41 · Leviathan, the King Over All the Children of Pride

precepts.text: The previous chapter opens Behemoth, the beast set to rule the earth, before chapter 41 turns to Leviathan of the sea.
precepts.point: He asks whether you can draw out Leviathan with a hook or his tongue with a cord, or put a hook into his nose or bore his jaw with a thorn, comparing this massive creature to fishing for a small fish. Leviathan is a massive, massive creature.

note.label: Job 41: Leviathan, the King Over All the Children of Pride

precepts.why:
The Most High is speaking about Leviathan, one of the beasts he created. He made two great beasts: Behemoth to rule the earth and Leviathan to rule the waters. The chapter before opens Behemoth: “Behold now behemoth, which I made with thee; he eateth grass as an ox.”

Then chapter 41 turns to Leviathan, the one that deals in the waters. “Canst thou draw out leviathan with an hook? or his tongue with a cord which thou lettest down?” He compares this massive creature to fishing for a small fish, putting a hook into his nose or boring his jaw through with a thorn. Leviathan is a massive, massive creature, made by the Most High just as Behemoth was.

Behemoth is the Enoch named in Esdras. Some Bibles suggest an elephant, but read the description. It eats grass like an ox, not meat. Its strength is in its loins and belly, and it moves its tail like a cedar, a great tree. An elephant's little tail is not like a cedar; this tail is so huge that a blow from it would kill a man.

Its sinews are bound together, its bones like strong brass and bars of iron. It is the chief of God's ways. Only the one who made it can bring his sword near it; no man can simply overpower this creature. That is why God separated Behemoth from Leviathan.

The mountains bring it food, matching Esdras's thousand hills, and the other beasts play there. It lies under shady trees among reeds and fens, with willows around it. It can drink up a river without hurrying and trusts that it can draw Jordan into its mouth. Other animals scatter when a lion comes to drink; Behemoth is not running from anything before it has finished. No snare man makes will capture it. That is not the description of an ordinary elephant.

points: Moreover the Lord answered Job and said, shall he that contendeth with the Almighty instruct Him? He that reproveth God, let him answer it.

note.label: Job 40: Humble Thyself Before the Most High

points: Then Job answered the Lord and said, behold, I am vile; what shall I answer Thee? I will lay mine hand upon my mouth. Once have I spoken, but I will not answer; yea, twice, but I will proceed no further. Job humbles himself and puts his hand over his mouth.

note.label: Job 40: Humble Thyself Before the Most High

points: The thing is we get so high-minded sometimes, because of the little bit of knowledge that we have out of this Bible, and the wicked still rule over us. You better humble yourself. That is the whole purpose of the book of Job: learning how to humble yourself.

note.label: Job 40: Humble Thyself Before the Most High

points: Then the Lord answered Job out of the whirlwind and said, gird up thy loins now like a man; I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto Me. Wilt thou also disannul My judgment? Wilt thou condemn Me, that thou mayest be righteous?

note.label: Job 40: Humble Thyself Before the Most High

points: The Most High is saying, if you can do these things, then can you disannul My judgment? Can you condemn the Most High, that you may be righteous? Can you bring down proud people? Can you get rid of the wicked?

note.label: Job 40: Humble Thyself Before the Most High

points: Hast thou an arm like God? Or canst thou thunder with a voice like Him? Deck thyself now with majesty and excellency, and array thyself with glory and beauty. Cast abroad the rage of thy wrath, and behold every one that is proud, and abase him. Look on every one that is proud, and bring him low, and tread down the wicked in their place.

note.label: Job 40: Humble Thyself Before the Most High

points: Behold now behemoth, which I made with thee; he eateth grass as an ox. His strength is in his loins, and his force is in the navel of his belly. He moveth his tail like a cedar; the sinews of his stones are wrapped together. His bones are as strong pieces of brass; his bones are like bars of iron.

He says his tail was like a cedar; a cedar is a very tall tree. There are not that many animals that have a tail the size of a cedar tree. A lot of people ask, where are the dinosaurs? Watch the video, The Beginning, Ending, and Midst of Times.

note.label: Job 40: Humble Thyself Before the Most High

points: He is the chief of the ways of God. He lieth under the shady trees, in the covert of the reed and fens. The willows of the brook compass him about. Behold, he drinketh up a river, and hasteth not; he trusteth that he can draw up Jordan into his mouth.
